results.reason: Issue 1 says the Varga stock purchase is a Change of Control requiring Crestline's prior written consent under §15.4. It says the Disclosure Schedule (Part 3.5) wrongly labels Crestline as 'Notice only; no consent required.' It explains the resulting termination right and fee, and that the §3.5 consents representation would be inaccurate, creating indemnity exposure.

Issue 7 notes that Crestline may assign to an Affiliate or Qualified Transferee on notice without consent, and that this 'could introduce a competitor of Varga.' It never analyzes the §1.1 Qualified Transferee definition (any Territory distributor of laboratory or diagnostic products). It also never explains that the definition does not exclude competitors of Halvorsen.

Issue 6 explains that the Amendment restates §12.3 so only Section 9 breaches are uncapped, dropping the §10 and §11 carve-outs, so those claims are now capped. It never invokes the §17.5 order-of-precedence clause as the reason the amendment controls.
The response states that the original §12.3 excluded from the caps breaches of Sections 9 and 10 and indemnification obligations under Section 11.
The response states that §12.2 caps aggregate liability at amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the preceding 12 months.
The response is a formal memo with separately numbered issues. Each issue has 'Where it appears' (document and section), 'Why it matters,' and 'Recommended fix.'
The response concludes that consent is required, not merely notice.
The response concludes that the §10 and §11 carve-outs were removed by the Amendment and those claims are now capped.
